paderborn_speed_channel_audit.signal_nature: Low-rate (4 kHz) analog/PLC speed estimate, NOT raw encoder pulse train.

cwru_speed_metadata_audit.signal_nature: Single scalar operating speed, NO continuous angle reference.

feasibility_assessment.cot_infeasibility_rationale: Genuine dynamic Computed Order Tracking (COT) requires synchronously recorded optical encoder pulses or a 1/rev keyphasor pulse train to reconstruct instantaneous shaft angle theta(t) via zero-crossing interpolation. CWRU provides only a single scalar nominal RPM (e.g. 1797). Simulating synthetic pulses is strictly prohibited by scientific integrity rules.
feasibility_assessment.nominal_order_scaling_rationale: Speed-normalized order-scaling (order = f / f_shaft_nominal) is technically feasible by re-interpolating the envelope spectrum onto a normalized shaft-order grid (orders 0 to 200). This normalizes for shaft rotational frequency differences between CWRU (29.95 Hz) and Paderborn (25.00 Hz).
feasibility_assessment.geometric_order_limitation: Even in the normalized order domain, defect orders differ because CWRU 6205 has 9 balls (BPFO = 3.585 orders, BPFI = 5.415 orders) while Paderborn 6203 has 8 balls (BPFO = 3.053 orders, BPFI = 4.947 orders).
